rows.title: Policy
rows.figure: Fed 3.75–4.00%, Dec hike ~70% (from ~84% after Oct 28); Logan: at least two more hikes; Musalem: hike needed soon; BoJ held 1.25% (8–1), Dec ~80%; ECB 2.50%, Dec hike likely; RBA Nov 3 ~79–85%; BoE Nov 5 ~94%; BoC Dec ~45%
rows.read: Most central banks still lean toward higher rates because energy keeps inflation high. Two Fed officials called for more hikes, yet markets trimmed the odds of a December hike as tech shares fell, so the dollar's rate edge is wobbling. The Bank of Japan held but moved closer to a December hike.

rows.title: Growth
rows.figure: Euro-area Q3 GDP +0.4% q/q (fc 0.2%): Germany +0.2%, France −0.1%, Italy 0.0%, Ireland +5.5%; Canada Aug GDP 0.0% (fc 0.2%); Chicago PMI 55.3 (fc 56.0); KOF 107.6 (fc 108.1)
rows.read: The euro area grew faster than expected over the summer, but mostly thanks to Ireland, with France shrinking and Italy flat. Canada's economy has stalled since before its rate hike, which weakens the case for another. US business activity is cooling a little from a fast pace.

rows.title: Inflation
rows.figure: German HICP 2.8% (fc 3.1%; Sep 3.3%); Italy CPI 5.4% (fc ~4.6%); France CPI 3.4%, HICP 3.8%; US ECI +0.8% q/q (in line), 3.4% y/y; Chicago prices paid highest since Dec 2021; BoJ FY2027 core forecast 2.6%
rows.read: Energy keeps prices high nearly everywhere, but unevenly: inflation cooled in Germany while it jumped in Italy and France. US wage growth held steady, so pay is not adding fresh pressure. Japan's central bank says underlying inflation has reached its goal.

rows.title: Risk
rows.read: A slide in big tech shares over AI spending sent money into US government bonds and the safe-haven currencies. That pulled US yields down, so the dollar slipped even as investors grew nervous. Gold got no safety boost and fell as some investors sold it to cover losses.

rows.title: Terms of trade
rows.figure: Brent $116.57 (+0.7%), WTI $104.15 (+2.1%); Gulf crude exports ~24.6m b/d mid-October; shipping ~$40/bbl; OPEC+ meets Sunday
rows.read: Oil stayed high as fear of new US strikes on Iran outweighed a recovery in Gulf exports. That keeps helping exporters like Canada and Australia and costing importers like Japan and the euro area.

rows.title: Positioning
rows.figure: CFTC Oct 20: funds strongly against CAD (sharply added), against NZD and EUR (euro net short largest since March 2020), for GBP and AUD (real money strongly against), strongly for gold
rows.read: Hedge funds hold their biggest bets against the Canadian dollar, and the loonie's climb since Canada's rate hike puts those bets under pressure. Their bets against the euro are the largest in years, so good euro news could force them to buy it back. Their big bets on gold are losing money as it slides.

rows.title: Fiscal
rows.figure: French revenue vote Nov 3; S&P reviews France Nov 27; France Q3 GDP −0.1%; UK Budget headroom £15bn
rows.read: France's budget fight is still unresolved and keeps a weight on the euro, with a vote on taxes due November 3. France's economy shrank over the summer, which makes its deficit harder to close. The UK Budget passed calmly, so the pound is trading on rates, not borrowing.
